current.text: Boozer is a rookie and is set to start for Memphis. Joe's projected starting five is Ty Jerome, Cedric Coward, Jerami Grant, Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey.
Ja Morant was traded to Portland, and Ty Jerome is expected to start at point guard.
With Morant gone, Boozer should take the first or second playmaking role in Memphis and his assist rate should go up. Experts see him as an excellent passer who can do more with the ball.
He is not expected to be a 30 usage player in the NBA.
Joe projects about 32 minutes a night, one of only two Grizzlies above 30 minutes. Another expert projects 30 minutes and says 33 minutes would make him an easy top 50 player.
Coach Tuomas Iisalo plays at a very high pace, uses short stints, keeps minutes down and runs an 11-man rotation on a deep roster.
In Summer League he averaged 17 points, 7 rebounds and 4 assists with a steal and a three, on 51% FG, 82% FT and 40% from three.
Experts expect him to struggle early, mostly with efficiency, like Cooper Flagg did, and to do more as the season goes on. He should play at a top 30 level by the fantasy playoffs.
Season-end call: at least a top 30 finish. He is the clear number one rookie this season.
Draft price: taking him in the 50s is fine, but inside the top 50 is early. In an auction mock, Josh's max was 15 USD and he went for 15 USD.
Because of how the Memphis roster is built, he will get every chance to win Rookie of the Year.

durable.text: He contributes in nearly every category: points, rebounds, assists, steals, solid free throws, good FG% and threes. Experts call his game scalable.
He has limits as a rim protector, and experts expect few blocks from him.
He plays more like a small forward than a center and has point forward potential.
He had a 30 usage rate at Duke with high assist numbers.
Turnovers are his weakest category and are high for a forward. Rebounds are his strongest category.

note: Experts price him in the 50s, and Josh's mock max of 15 USD is close to Yahoo's 14.8 USD average cost. ESPN's 4 USD value is far below where experts put him, so he can come cheap if our room follows ESPN. He fits punt TO builds, and his rebounds, points and passing as a forward help most builds. Early in the season, check his minutes under Iisalo's short stints, his assist share with Morant gone, and his efficiency. Experts expect a slow start, so hold him through a weak first month.
